questions.question: What does standard form do to the coefficients in a linear system?
options: It moves all constants to the left and deletes them.
It removes all variables from the system.
It requires every coefficient to be $1$.
It lines them up by variable across the equations.

questions.question: What is the general standard-form equation for row $i$ of a system with unknowns $x_1,\ldots,x_n$?
options: $a_{1i}x_i=b_i$ only.
$x_i=a_{i1}+a_{i2}+\cdots+a_{in}$.
$a_{i1}x_1+a_{i2}x_2+\cdots+a_{in}x_n=b_i$.

questions.question: How are missing variables handled in standard form?
options: They are renamed as parameters immediately.
They make the system nonlinear.
They are moved to the right-hand side.
They are given coefficient $0$.

questions.question: Which objects are obtained from a system once it is in standard form?
options: The coefficient matrix $A$ and right-hand side vector $b$.
The basis of the solution set without solving.
The eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
The determinant and inverse of every matrix.

questions.question: Write $2x+5=3y$ in standard form with unknowns $x,y$.
options: $2x=3y-5$ only.
$3y-2x=5$ only.

questions.question: In standard form for unknowns $x,y,z$, what coefficient is used for $y$ in $x+2z=7$?
Why is $x+y=1$ and $2x-y=0$ easy to encode as $Ax=b$?
options: The system has no right-hand side constants, so $b$ is the zero vector.
The coefficients of $x$ and $y$ are already aligned by variable.
The equations are nonlinear.
There are more unknowns than equations.

questions.question: Why is $x_1x_2+x_3=0$ not a row of a linear system in standard form?
options: It has the constant $0$ on the right.
It uses subscripted variables.
It has three unknowns.
It contains a product of unknowns.

questions.question: Why is standard form a convention rather than a new mathematical problem?
options: It changes the solution set on purpose.
It solves the system directly, so no row operations are needed after writing it in standard form.
It adds new unknowns to every equation.
It reorganizes the same linear equations so their coefficients can be read systematically.

questions.question: If the unknown order is changed, why might two correct coefficient matrices look different?
options: Because their columns follow different variable orders.
Because the number of equations changes.
Because the right-hand side vector must become zero.
Because standard form allows arbitrary nonlinear terms.

questions.question: For $3y-2z=5$ with unknown order $x,y,z$, which standard-form row is correct?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&3&-2\end{pmatrix}$ with right-hand side $5$.
$\begin{pmatrix}3&-2&0\end{pmatrix}$ with right-hand side $5$.
$\begin{pmatrix}5&0&3\end{pmatrix}$ with right-hand side $-2$.
$\begin{pmatrix}0&3&5\end{pmatrix}$ with right-hand side $-2$.

questions.question: Write $2x-3=4y+z$ in standard form with unknowns $x,y,z$.
options: $4y+z-2x=-3$ only.
